title: Rodrigo Duterte camp opposes 'sweeping' closed sessions for ICC prosecution witnesses
summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - Former President Rodrigo Duterte"s defense team opposes the International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecution"s request for a “sweeping use” of closed court sessions for…

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – Former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team opposes the International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecution’s request for a “sweeping use” of closed court sessions for witnesses, arguing it “unjustifiably infringes” upon his right to a public trial.

Duterte’s counsel Peter Haynes and his team state a “deep concern” over the scope of the Office of the Prosecutor’s (OTP) request for anonymity for most of its witnesses, and that the “same objectively justifiable risk” is not established in each witness category.

“The Prosecution is requesting that 55 out of the 69 of its witnesses testify anonymously, including 32 insiders. Further, it asks that 22 witnesses be authorised to give evidence entirely in closed session,” Haynes noted in a redacted filing released on November 23.
“Simply put, the Prosecution is requesting anonymity for 79% of its testifying witnesses, 40% of whom would then give evidence effectively in secret.”

Haynes argues that the high-profile status, increased media exposure, being government members or PNP officers, living in the Philippines or in the same area as Duterte’s supporters, or being known to the former president are “insufficient reasons, per se, to warrant protective measures.”

Duterte’s defense team asks Trial Chamber III to consider the “necessary and proportionate implementation” of using pseudonyms and face/voice distortions. It also raises “less stringent measures” such as the “targeted use of private sessions”.
“[T]hat would neutralise or mitigate the alleged risks to the same extent all the while respecting Mr Duterte’s rights,” Haynes noted.

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang has requested special in-court security measures to “protect the witness’s (or another person’s) safety, physical and psychological well-being, dignity, and privacy”.

He argues these protections are warranted “in light of the high vulnerability of these witnesses,” or to “minimize the impact of testimony by providing psychological and emotional support to the witnesses.”

Although the Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV) back the prosecution’s request due to “prevailing political and social climate in the Philippines”, they suggest the court adopt a “comprehensive and prospective approach” in its assessment to prevent a “real risk of harm, intimidation and/or social ostracism” to witnesses and their families.
The defense’s opposition comes a few days before Duterte’s ICC trial opens, with limited public information on which prosecution witnesses Trial Chamber III will allow to appear in court.
Presiding judge Joanna Korner and fellow judges Keebong Paek and Nicolas Guillou have yet to publicly release their decision on protective measures for witnesses admitted in court. — BAP, GMA News
